paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage hands you. Hezekiah had just been healed, and envoys came from Babylon with letters and a gift, and he showed them EVERYTHING. When Isaiah asked what they had seen, Hezekiah answered, "There is nothing among my treasures that I did not show them." (2 Kings 20:15). I think it's easy to pour the whole heart into what we own when life is going great.

Then comes the part that gets me. The LORD says through Isaiah that everything in the palace will be carried off to Babylon (2 Kings 20:17), and Hezekiah answers, "The word of the LORD that you have spoken is good." (2 Kings 20:19). I think he was looking only at his own days, since the text says he thought, "Will there not at least be peace and security in my lifetime?" (2 Kings 20:19). Baker, I know that feeling, staring at my own cozy counter and never thinking about who sits there next.

So here's the big idea. The treasure Hezekiah was so proud to show off was going to be carried away to Babylon, just as the LORD said (2 Kings 20:17). What we hold in our hands is not what we should hold tightest. Ask yourself today what you're showing off and what you're really trusting.
